description: JACL Milestone 6 — Line-Based Syntax Sugar: Implicit brackets for bare commands, comma/semicolon/newline command separators, backslash line continuation, bare words and $var at statement position desugar to zero-arg command calls

userStories.title: Comma token in lexer
userStories.description: As the lexer, I need to emit TOKEN_COMMA when encountering ',' so the parser can use it as a command separator.
acceptanceCriteria: Add TOKEN_COMMA to the TokenType enum (between TOKEN_SEMICOLON and TOKEN_WORD)
Lexer emits TOKEN_COMMA for ',' characters — same pattern as TOKEN_SEMICOLON in the single-character delimiters section of lexer_lex()
Comma inside strings is not tokenized (already handled — string body lexer consumes string content)
Update the lexer header comment from '23 token types' to reflect the new count
Unit test: 'def x 1, def y 2' lexes to [WORD WORD INT COMMA WORD WORD INT EOF]
Unit test: a comma inside a string literal '"a,b"' produces TOKEN_STRING, not TOKEN_COMMA
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Backslash line continuation in lexer
userStories.description: As the lexer, I need to consume '\' followed by a newline as whitespace so that long commands can span multiple lines.
acceptanceCriteria: When '\' is immediately followed by '\n' (or '\r\n'), the lexer consumes both characters and emits no token — continues lexing the next line as part of the same logical line

Implementation: in the operator character section of lexer_lex(), when the first char is '\', peek ahead — if next is '\n' or '\r\n', consume the backslash + newline, increment lex->line, reset lex->col to 1, and continue (no token emitted)
'\' followed by something other than a newline continues to be lexed as an operator character (existing behavior — '\' is in lexer__is_operator_char)
Line counter (lex->line) is incremented and column resets to 1 after consuming backslash-newline
Unit test: 'puts \\\nhello' (backslash-newline) lexes to [WORD WORD EOF] with hello on line 2
Unit test: 'puts \\\r\nhello' — CRLF continuation works, lexes to [WORD WORD EOF]
Backslash continuation inside strings is unaffected (strings have their own escape handling in lexer__lex_string_body)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Comma as command separator in parser
userStories.description: As the parser, I need to treat TOKEN_COMMA as a command terminator (like newlines and semicolons) so users can write multiple commands on one line separated by commas.
acceptanceCriteria: parser__is_command_end returns true for TOKEN_COMMA (add to the condition alongside TOKEN_NEWLINE, TOKEN_SEMICOLON, TOKEN_EOF, TOKEN_RBRACE)
Top-level parsing loop in parser_parse() skips TOKEN_COMMA between commands (add TOKEN_COMMA to the while condition that already skips TOKEN_NEWLINE and TOKEN_SEMICOLON)
Block parsing loop in parser__parse_block() skips TOKEN_COMMA between commands (add TOKEN_COMMA to the while condition that already skips TOKEN_NEWLINE and TOKEN_SEMICOLON)
Integration test: 'def x 1, def y 2, [+ $x $y]' evaluates to 3 via jacl_run()
Integration test: '{ def a 10, def b 20, [+ $a $b] }' in a block evaluates to 30
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Bare words as zero-arg command calls
userStories.description: As the parser, I need to treat a bare word alone at statement position as a zero-arg command call, so that 'exit' on its own line desugars to '[exit]'.
acceptanceCriteria: In parser__parse_bare_command, when args.count == 0 and head->type is AST_LIT_STRING (bare word), wrap head in a new AST_COMMAND node with arg_count = 0 — instead of returning head directly
'exit' parses to AST_COMMAND { head: AST_LIT_STRING("exit"), args: [], arg_count: 0 } — same structure as '[exit]'
'puts hello' still parses to AST_COMMAND { head: AST_LIT_STRING("puts"), args: [AST_LIT_STRING("hello")] } — multi-word lines are unchanged
Bare words inside brackets remain string literals: in '[puts exit]', 'exit' is parsed by parser__parse_atom as AST_LIT_STRING — not affected by this change
A bare integer alone on a line (42) is NOT wrapped — remains AST_LIT_INT
A bare float alone on a line (3.14) is NOT wrapped — remains AST_LIT_FLOAT
A bare quoted string alone ('"hello"') is NOT wrapped — remains AST_LIT_STRING
A bracketed command alone ('[foo]') is returned directly from parser__parse_expr — not double-wrapped
A block alone ('{ ... }') is returned directly — not wrapped as a call
Unit tests verify each case via ParseResult AST node inspection
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: $var lines as command calls
userStories.description: As the parser, I need to treat $var alone at statement position as a zero-arg call, so that '$fn' on its own line desugars to '[$fn]'.
acceptanceCriteria: In parser__parse_bare_command, when args.count == 0 and head->type is AST_VAR_REF, wrap head in a new AST_COMMAND node with arg_count = 0
'$fn' parses to AST_COMMAND { head: AST_VAR_REF("fn"), args: [], arg_count: 0 }
'$fn 1 2' parses to AST_COMMAND { head: AST_VAR_REF("fn"), args: [1, 2] } — this already works via the existing multi-arg path
$var inside brackets remains a variable reference: '[puts $x]' — $x is parsed by parser__parse_atom and is unchanged
Integration test: 'proc greet [] { 42 }\ndef f greet\n$f' evaluates to 42
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Update existing tests for new bare-word semantics
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to verify that existing tests still pass with the new bare-word-as-call semantics and update any tests that relied on bare words being string literals at statement position.
acceptanceCriteria: Run the full existing test suite: test_lexer, test_parser, test_compiler, test_vm, test_m4, test_m5, test_integration, test_value, test_string, test_bytecode
Identify any tests that fail due to: (a) bare words at statement position now being AST_COMMAND instead of AST_LIT_STRING, or (b) TOKEN_COMMA being a new token type
Update failing tests to match new semantics — e.g., parser tests that asserted a bare word at top level was AST_LIT_STRING should now assert AST_COMMAND
All existing tests pass after updates
No regressions in bracket-based code behavior — any test using [cmd ...] syntax should produce identical results
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: End-to-end M6 integration tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need comprehensive integration tests in test/test_m6.c that verify the full pipeline (lex -> parse -> compile -> run) for line-based syntax.
acceptanceCriteria: test/test_m6.c exists using jacl_run() and PrintCapture pattern from previous milestones
Test: bare command with args — 'puts hello' compiles and runs like '[puts hello]'
Test: bare command no args — 'exit' produces AST_COMMAND with arg_count 0 (verified via parser_parse)
Test: $var command — 'proc f [] { 42 }\ndef g f\n$g' evaluates to 42
Test: semicolon separator — 'def x 1; def y 2; [+ $x $y]' evaluates to 3
Test: comma separator — 'def x 10, def y 20, [+ $x $y]' evaluates to 30
Test: mixed separators — 'def a 1; def b 2, def c 3\n[+ [+ $a $b] $c]' evaluates to 6
Test: backslash continuation — 'def x \\\n42\n$x' evaluates to 42
Test: continuation in block — '{ def x 1, def y 2, [+ $x $y] }' evaluates to 3
Test: nested brackets in line mode — 'puts [+ 1 [* 2 3]]' works correctly
Test: explicit brackets still work — '[def x 42]\n[+ $x 1]' evaluates to 43
Test: proc definition line-based — 'proc add [a b] { [+ $a $b] }\nadd 3 4' evaluates to 7
Test file added to build.sh TESTS array as 'test/test_m6.c|test_m6'
All tests pass
M6 row in DESIGN.md milestone table status updated from empty to **COMPLETE**
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99
